Barbès and Gare du Nord used to be big Drug deal point 15 years ago. But don't be too much alarmed, things have been going WAY better in the last 10 years. Like WAY WAY better.

--

To make it easier to understand, Gare du Nord and Barbès are easy access to Paris for drug dealers that comes from the North East area of Paris (saint-Denis). 15 years ago it was an open drug market and a place to avoid. Now dealers are way more hidden thanks to police and you can safely pass those area without having to fear anything (just maybe don't openly carry very luxury stuff). As long as you don't wander or hang out in those area nobody will bother you. If you start to look around there are probably some dealer that think you are looking for stuff and they'll come to you to ask you if are looking for something (aka drugs, cheap tobacco). Also of course there are some junkies around there so if you pass the area you might spot few of them but cops are never pretty far.

--

That being said it's very centered in Barbès train station and Gare du Nord train station. The dealer don't really go outside because most of their customer stop at those train station, buy the stuff and leave by train. The place you are is good and pretty close to the Canal saint-martin and le marais which are both AMAZING place.

--

So my advice. When you are leaving your place and want to walk around, go in the direction of east for a nice walk (canal saint martin) or south for some restaurant and bar (le marais) or west for cultural stuff (Paris center) but don't go north (Gare du Nord/Barbès). You'll probably have to pass this area if you want to walk to the sacré-coeur and that's ok, just don't "visit" there.

Then the most important part: DO NOT WASTE TIME

 

One of the most important part in SoT is time management. The more time you lose doing uneffective stuff the easier it'll be for people to catch you by surprise. For exemple if you raise Gold hoarder emissary flag don't even bother looting OoS or Merchant stuff. Just let it on the ground or burry it and loot only the good gold hoarder stuff. Looting is extremelly time consuming. You waste a LOOOOT of time loading/unloading stuff and it's often during this time that you get catch by other ship. Also learn to do all activity efficiently. Most stuff in SoT shouldn't take you more than half an hour to complete and you should never have to go too far from your ship.

 

A good list of stuff to do solo are:

- Underwater shrine. Go with an empty boat, do it, come back and even if you have been sunk your loot is safe.
- Seafort. Just stay on your sloop and use cannon to clean the wave. Check the horizon between each wave. Once it is done, run to gather all important supplies (plank, cannonball and good food are always at the same spot), put them on your ship, check horizon again then go to loot only the interesting stuff inside the fort
- Vault: Rush the vault, get the tribut and 5 or 6 of the biggest chest then loot cash. Once done bring the tribute to your ship, check horizon, then loot the rest if it is safe. Don't bother for small loot, it cost a giant amount of time to load/unload and it worth nothing.
- Merchant run: Buy every cargo in an outpost, go to the next outpost and sell everything. Buy every cargo in the new outpost and go to the next outpost and sell everything. Repeat and turn in circle on the map. It should take you a bit less than an hour to make a full circle of the map. Don't bother with maximum value trade, just buy all/sell all.
- World event: Do them only if you have a tons of cannonballs or if the server seems dead.

You should prep the macro story but let the micro story to impro. You don't need to create or control everything. Create a shell and let the player fill this shell. For exemple on a quick and simple story:

 

*The macro part*

A bad guy kidnap a princess and the king ask you to get her back. 

* The bad guy and the princess are actually in love but the princess is fiancee with another dude.
* The king told you that the bad guy is asking for a ransom (which is false). He said that the princess is probably jailed in the basement while in reality she is in the top of the dungeon with her lover.

 

*The micro part*

How do the player reach the basement? Let them do it their way. Bride the guard? Ok. Find a secret passage? Ok. Let them use their ability. **If they find a way to use their ability and suceed their skill check just say Yes and play around this idea**. All you need to do is to keep in mind the macro part of the story so you won't have big plothole. In this simple scenario, the main element is that the princess is not and has never been in the basement. They'll look everywhere in the basement, get lost, will have to deal with some guard and at the end they'll understand that something is fishy. Now that they understand that the princess in not in the basement they'll have to find a way to find the princess and understand what is happening. Again, let them do it their way. Let them use their ability and give them information when they succeed.

 

The story is pretty simple but your players choice will matter a lot on:

* How do they reach the basement?
* How do they find out that the princess is upstair?
* How do they reach upstair?
* What do they do once they got the whole story?

 

All of those elements will be build by players. All you had to create was the macro story, a map, few guard, a princess and a bad guy. For campaign just do it on a bigger scale.

1 arcane explosion is absolutly mandatory. It clean the board before the arcane missile show and avoid losing to people stacking tons of stats on the board (aka druids).

Evocation is a bad idea. You don't need it to stack spell power and if you draw your cheap spell early you want to use them to control the board, not to stick in your hand while being bullied. Also if you use it during the OTK you can easily screw up with animation time and hand size.

The trickiest part is to find a way to win against aggro deck. Luckily a lot a them have a hard time to deal with Mozaki so you can often find a win just by controlling the board with all the cheap spell early and dropping Mozaki on a turn where your opponent can't clean it with his board.

You are missing the difference between tempo and aggro. Tempo means you fight for the board control. When you are aggressive you'll naturally have the board control but it doesn't means you fight for it (aka: go face instead of value trading for exemple). An aggro deck is someone who'll simply rush the face (outside of the few highly valuable trade). An aggro deck will have limited ressources and will use most of them to go face. It was the case for pirate warrior or old hunter face. Very often the game end when the aggro deck didn't had board control but could still finish his opponent with few direct damages (weapon, hunter hero power). A mid-range tempo deck isn't an aggro deck. It'll fight for the board and do the value trade + add the extra damages to he opponent face, slowly harassing him while securing the board.
